issue.body:
## Problem

- Workflow owners need saved views they can select, change, reset and share from the redesigned list.
- Revives https://github.com/Silthus/posthog/pull/401, parked on the fork. Builds on the API in [#129290](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/129290).

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🔵 **Merge risk: low** · two-way door (merge-risk rubric), graded with the flag off
> - Flag off, none of this renders and the list sends no `workflow_views` request.
> - Flag on, a wrong conflict path could drop a teammate's view. Stale writes get 409.
> - **Revert:** turn off `workflows-list-v2`.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

- With `workflows-list-v2` on, saved-view tabs sit above the folder list, with save, rename, delete, reset and conflict handling.
- A view's own filters and the user's added filters look different, and Update view saves the additions in place.
- Search text typed on a view stays when the user picks another view, like an added filter. It marks the view as changed, Reset discards it, and Update view saves it. A reload keeps it.
- Delete asks for confirmation and says everyone in the project loses the view.
- A view link shows a loading list, with no rows to act on, until the saved views load.
- Columns come from the view and its link and are no longer kept in the browser, so a view link always shows the view's columns.
- Leaving the list and coming back restores the view, its added filters and its columns. A view link opens the view, even over filters kept from an earlier visit.
- A rename or update that a teammate's save makes stale answers 409, and the toast points at Reset. The rename dialog closes so Reset is in reach.
- Saving shows "Saving the view...", and Undo still works during a save.
- Filters added during a save or while a view link loads stay.

</details>

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bb938e7-65fa-477a-a7c3-370409c03aae

The whole stack from the user's side: finding a workflow in a long list, then saved views and folders. Recorded on the full stack (#129167 to #129291) merged locally, with invented data. Voiced and captioned.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `workflowsSavedViewsLogic.test.ts` catches lost edits on conflict, 404 and pending saves. The tab tests catch broken keyboard overflow.

New this round: a view link's columns win over columns kept in the browser, and an empty project shows the setup page. Earlier stages cover a view link while the views load, rename, a 409 conflict recovered with Reset, views that fail to load and then Retry, and delete confirmation. A saved view's search text comes back when the view is picked again, and typed text carries to the next view and saves with Update view. Typed text that matches a view's saved search keeps Reset and survives a reload. Flags off before and after use: plain list, no `workflow_views` request, API 403.

issue.body:
## Problem

- Teams without a verified sending domain can't send transactional email from code, even to their own team.
- With #131834, a code send on the sandbox sender queues, then fails.

## Changes

- A code send from the team's `email_sandbox` sender goes out through the sandbox path: member checks, caps, retries, no billing.
- The 202 and keyed replays carry `sender_kind: "email_sandbox"`.
- Refusals: non-member 422; cc, bcc, reply-to or custom from 400; blocked, paused or foreign sandbox sender 403.
- A keyed retry without a from address replays after Django resolved another sender.
- A keyed retry replays across the deploy: keys store both fingerprint shapes.
- A new sandbox sender missing from the replica is read from the primary.
- Sandbox code sends carry no open or click tracking.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    A1[code send] --> B1[email queue] --> C1[email service: refused]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[code send] --> B2[email queue] --> D2[sandbox queue] --> E2[sandbox SES]
  end

```

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - Keyed code sends without a from address, on any sender, in both regions: a wrong fingerprint match replays instead of sending.
> - **Switch-off:** `WORKFLOWS_SANDBOX_SENDER_ENABLED` for the sandbox path; the fingerprint change is live on deploy, fix forward.

## Rollout

- **Stages:** Node live in both regions before the Django change that sends sandbox sender ids.
- **Watch:** reserve `conflict` in `cdp_hogflow_idempotency_operations_total`; no alert pages on it.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `sandbox-code-send.test.ts` drives the endpoint and workers into a fake SES; each case failed first. One `cdp-api.serial.test.ts` row moved from conflict to replay.

- Proofs at bbab7cbb: live run and cross-version, below.
- CI: the schema-check failure in `Node.js parallel Tests` comes from #131834.

<details>
<summary>Proof evidence</summary>

- **Live run:** a member send through the sandbox path reached a local SES stand-in; a non-member got 422; a keyed retry replayed with one message sent.
- **Cross-version**, against the parent PR's head: keyed retries replay in both directions, and own-sender sends deliver. A sandbox send run by old workers fails without sending, so the deploy order holds.

</details>

- Not checked: a live send against real SES.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/qa-swarm`, `/pr-description`, `/merge-risk`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** T3 Code implementation lane; Claude Code with Jest, tsc and the Fleet heavy runner.
- **Decisions:** the endpoint checks the sender's team and kind; the worker routes a `function_email` step with `state.senderKind` to the sandbox handler.
- **Decisions:** a failed membership or tenant read lets the send queue; the sandbox worker rechecks and retries.
- **Decisions:** the workflow email quota check still applies to sandbox sends.
- **Follow-ups:** the message status row of a sandbox code send stays at queued; the sandbox path writes no status rows.
- **Follow-ups:** retire the previous fingerprint shape. One key lifetime (24 hours) after this is live in both regions, write the current shape into `fingerprint`; drop the previous shape in a later deploy.

+      content.delete("\r\n").unpack1('m0')
+    rescue ArgumentError, EncodingError
+      raise invalid("An attachment's content is text that isn't Base64. Pass the file's bytes, read with " \
+                    'File.binread, or the file encoded as Base64.', field)
+    end
+
+    def self.wrapped_base64?(content)
+      text = content.delete("\r").chomp
+      width = text.index("\n")
+      return true if width.nil?
+
+      text.ascii_only? && BASE64_LINE_WIDTHS.include?(width) && lines_of_width?(text, width)
+    end
+
+    def self.lines_of_width?(text, width)
+      line_break = width
+      while (next_break = text.index("\n", line_break + 1))
+        return false unless next_break == line_break + width + 1
+
+        line_break = next_break
+      end
+      (text.length - line_break - 1).between?(1, width)
+    end
+
+    def self.invalid(message, field)
+      EmailError.new(code: 'invalid_attachment', message: message, field: field)
+    end
+
+    def self.too_many_files
+      EmailError.new(code: 'too_many_attachments', field: 'attachments',
+                     message: "An email carries at most #{MAX_FILES} files, so no email was sent.",
+                     why: "An email carries at most #{MAX_FILES} files.",
+                     fix: "Attach at most #{MAX_FILES} files, and link to any others from the email body.")
+    end
+
+    private_class_method :new, :attachment, :check_keys, :file_bytes, :raw_bytes, :base64_bytes,
+                         :wrapped_base64?, :lines_of_width?, :invalid, :too_many_files
+
+    def initialize(attachments, bodies)
+      @attachments = attachments
+      check_size(bodies)
+    end
+
+    def empty?
+      @attachments.empty?
+    end
+
+    # @return [Array<Hash>] The files as the send names them.
+    def references
+      @attachments.map { |attachment| { 'sha256' => attachment.sha256 }.merge(attachment.reference) }
+    end
+
+    # @return [Array<Attachment>] Each distinct file once, in the order the caller gave them.
+    def distinct
+      @attachments.uniq(&:sha256)
+    end
+
+    private
+
+    def check_size(bodies)
+      return if message_bytes(bodies) <= MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES
+
+      raise EmailError.new(
+        code: 'message_too_large', field: 'attachments',
+        message: 'The files are too large for one email, so no email was sent.',
+        why: "PostHog's email provider takes emails up to 40 MB, and Base64 encoding makes each file about a " \
+             'third larger.',
+        fix: "Keep the email under #{LIMIT}: attach fewer or smaller files, or link to large files from the email " \
+             'body.'
+      )
+    end
+
+    def message_bytes(bodies)
+      files = @attachments.sum { |attachment| encoded_bytes(attachment.bytes.bytesize) }
+      files + bodies.sum { |body| encoded_bytes(utf8_bytesize(body)) } + HEADERS_AND_MIME_BOUNDARIES_BYTES
comment.body: Not changing this. The estimate has to match PostHog's count exactly, and PostHog's count (spec #71's "Message estimate", node-store's `estimateMessageBytes`) is each file, `html` and `text` at their Base64 size with line breaks, plus a flat 64 KiB for headers, the subject included. So the server doesn't refuse the case described. If the SDK counted the subject on top, it would refuse emails that PostHog accepts.

issue.title: Make the MCP gateway its own pack.ts pack, served from the hub
issue.body:
## Problem

The MCP gateway lives inside the Hub pack, so it can only be turned on with all of the hub's other work. Each machine's key also comes from someone running `fleet mcphub grant` by hand on the hub, and that includes the hub itself. Fleet v2 step 2 makes the gateway the first served hub service (`docs/architecture.md` D11, D12, D14): the hub issues its own key during apply, and the bridge reads that key with `ctx.use`.

This is step 2.4 of 4. Merge [#31](https://github.com/Silthus/fleet-engine/pull/31) first.

## Merge Danger

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - Every machine whose profile lists the Hub pack moves its gateway entries from `hub` to the new `mcp-gateway` pack at its next apply. The key names stay `fleet-hub`, so agents keep the same MCP server name. The value now starts `fleet mcp-connect` instead of `fleet mcphub connect`.
> - `fleet mcphub` goes. A devbox or Mac that holds only today's client file moves its key into the secret store at its next apply, and the bridge then reads the key from the store. A box gets both files from the hub at handover.
> - On the hub, apply now runs the gateway's install as a Fleet repair whenever the install check fails. Before, the install ran as a step after the adapters.
> - A hub whose gateway was installed at its HTTPS host gets it reinstalled at loopback at its next apply: one container restart, with sign-ins and keys kept. Its upstream sign-ins then go through `coder port-forward`.
> - Every `fleet` error that reaches the top level now goes to standard error instead of standard output.
> - **Switch-off:** set `workflows: { "mcp-gateway": false }` in the profile. Otherwise there is no switch-off: it is live on deploy, and we fix forward.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Summary

- **`packs/mcp-gateway` is a `pack.ts` pack.** It has one default-on workflow, `mcp-gateway`, and these items:
  - The served service `mcp-gateway/mcp-gateway`: on the hub, Linux, port 3317, health `/health`. It has no process, because Docker's restart policy keeps the container up. Its credential is today's per-machine `grant` key (`Fleet <node>`, scoped to the `fleet` group).
  - The install check `mcp-gateway-installed`: on the hub, Linux. Its test is a quiet doctor. Its Fleet repair is today's install.
  - The client check `mcp-gateway-client` on every node. It passes when the store holds a key, `~/.config/fleet/mcphub.client.json` holds the same key, and `/health` answers at loopback. Its Fleet repair writes the client file from the store. When the store is empty, the repair moves the key from today's client file into the store.
  - The Claude and Codex entries `fleet-hub`, which start `fleet mcp-connect`.
- **`fleet mcp-connect`** is today's stdio bridge. It gets the URL and key from `ctx.use`.
- **`fleet mcp-gateway`** is the hub's administration:
  - `doctor`, the default, as before.
  - `sign-in` prints `coder port-forward <hub> --tcp 3317` for your computer and each pending upstream authorization URL. It writes no redirect page.
  - `reconnect <server>` and `restart`.
  - `grant <machine>` and its `accept` stay until step 3 pulls keys. `grant` on the hub's own name saves the key to the store and the client file.
- **The order inside apply's gate changes.** Apply first tests the checks that served services wait for, then issues credentials, then runs the other Fleet repairs. So on the hub's first apply, the client check's repair writes the client file from the new key. Credentials are issued on the hub and on a solo machine (`plan.onHub`). Before, only a machine with the hub role got them.
- **`ctx.stdin()`** gives a command its standard input. The bridge and `accept` read from it.
- **A profile that lists the Hub pack gets the `mcp-gateway` pack** until it sets `workflows: { "mcp-gateway": false }`. That flag is the same one that turned the gateway off before.
- **The Hub pack** loses the gateway's workflow, its step, check, and config items, and `fleet mcphub`. Its other modules now import the client helpers from `packs/mcp-gateway/lib`. Box handover also writes the key to the box's store, and a spawned box checks its key with `fleet run mcp-gateway/mcp-gateway-client`.
- `docs/architecture.md` describes the pack as built. The page is regenerated: the `mcp-gateway` pack appears after the Hub pack, with the moment that it had before.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** `packs/mcp-gateway/pack.test.ts` drives `fleet` through `main` on a temporary home with the real engine. The MCPHub API and the gateway's MCP endpoint are faked at `fetch`. Docker is faked at `Bun.spawn`, and every other process runs for real.
  - **On the hub:**
    - The first apply issues `Fleet hub-1` once, stores it, and writes the client file with mode 600. Codex gets the `mcp-connect` entry.
    - `fleet mcp-connect` then sends `initialize` with `Bearer <issued key>` and prints the gateway's answer.
    - A second apply issues nothing new.
  - **A gateway that does not answer:** apply runs the install repair (the first Docker call is `docker image inspect fleet-mcphub:1.1.0-…`) and issues no key. The bridge then exits 1 and says to apply on the hub.
  - **Sign-in** prints the forward line with the profile's hub and the pending URL.
  - **A solo machine** issues its own key.
  - **On a devbox:**
    - Apply moves today's client file's key into the store, and the bridge uses it.
    - Without a key, apply names the client check.
    - `accept` saves the key from stdin, and the check then passes.
    - The install check never runs there.
  - **Plan tests:**
    - Every node's catalog holds `mcp-gateway/mcp-gateway 3317 /health`.
    - Each AI plan gets only its own provider's entry, owned by `mcp-gateway`, with no host or key in it.
    - A profile that lists the Hub pack keeps the gateway, and the workflow flag turns it off.
  - **Hub pack tests:**
    - Box handover sends the key for the store on stdin, and never in argv.
    - The property test (no item points at a hub without the Hub pack) now also leaves out `mcp-gateway`.
- **Red, then green:** on #31's head, 9 of the 10 pack tests fail. The tenth checks that a devbox runs no install, and it already passes there. All 10 pass on this head. Each of these mutants fails a test:
  - issuing after the other repairs;
  - dropping solo from `onHub`;
  - dropping the carried pack;
  - dropping the key move or the file write in the client repair;
  - dropping the box's store copy;
  - dropping `accept`'s store write;
  - dropping `ctx.stdin`;
  - dropping `on: "hub"` from the install check.
- **Review fixes, red then green.** Each new test failed before its fix and passes after it:
  - A devbox client file at the hub's old HTTPS address gives its key to the store and moves to loopback.
  - A gateway installed at an HTTPS address fails the install check, and apply runs the install repair.
  - With a file where the pack's state folder should be, `fleet mcp-connect` writes nothing to standard output and sends `fleet: EEXIST…` to standard error.
  - `fleet mcp-gateway grant hub-1` through `fleet` writes the store and the client file, and the bridge then uses the key. A mutant without either write fails this test. It replaces the unit test that spied on `saveKey`.
- **Lane gate:** `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run test` on this head, with `main` merged in: 1652 pass. 15 fail only on the devbox that built this, as they do on `main` there: three tracker tests, because its Git allowlist rewrites https origins, and twelve privacy-scan tests, because it has no gitleaks build.
- **CI:** pending on the head.
- **Gaps:** these run live after the merge:
  - a sign-in through the Mac's `coder port-forward`;
  - the first apply on the real hub;
  - a devbox apply that moves its key into the store.

## Decisions

See the decision comment below.

Involvement: one GPT-6.1 Sol review round. It found two blocking issues and two should-fix issues, and all four are fixed with tests. A second GPT-6.1 Sol round over the stack's fix commits and its merges from `main` found one should-fix, in #28: an outage now also removes a gated key that overlaps an older one. It is fixed with a test. No live proof was captured: Michael's overnight order on 2026-11-10 moves live proofs to follow-ups after the merge.

## For reviewers

The merge from `main` points the Recovery pack's `Fetch` type import at `packs/mcp-gateway/lib/client.ts`, because this PR moves that file.


This is PR 4 of 4 for Fleet v2 step 2. Most of the diff moves files from `packs/hub/lib/mcphub` and `packs/hub/mcphub` to `packs/mcp-gateway`. The first commit holds the moves only. The new code is in `pack.ts`, `lib/host.ts`, the client check in `lib/client.ts`, `issueKey` and `signIn` in `lib/hub.ts`, the gate order in `src/reconciler/apply.ts`, and `carriedPacks` and `onHub` in `src/reconciler/resolve.ts`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comment.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Michael**

**Decision lines** (overnight run: the worker took the recommended option and recorded it here)

- 🤖 **When does the hub issue its key on its first apply?** Inside the gate: apply tests the checks that served services wait for, issues the credentials, then runs the other Fleet repairs. So the client check's repair writes today's client file from the new key in the same apply, and a rerun changes nothing.
- 🤖 **Who issues credentials?** The machine that runs the hub's items: the hub, or a solo machine (`plan.onHub`). Before, only the hub role did, so a solo machine's bridge had no key.
- 🤖 **What keeps existing Hub-pack profiles working?** A profile that lists the Hub pack gets the `mcp-gateway` pack until it sets `workflows: { "mcp-gateway": false }`, the same flag that turned the gateway off before. Without it, every machine would lose its MCP entries at the next update.
- 🤖 **How do devboxes and Macs keep their keys until stack 3 pulls them?** The client check's Fleet repair moves the key from today's client file into the empty store. Box handover writes both files. `fleet mcp-gateway grant` and `accept` stay until stack 3.
- 🤖 **How does the bridge get stdin?** The SDK gains `ctx.stdin()`. The bridge writes protocol lines through `ctx.print` and errors to standard error.
- 🤖 **Which address does the gateway's sign-in use?** Loopback only. The install no longer reads `hub.httpsHost`, and sign-in prints the `coder port-forward` line, as the spec says. Admin commands rely on the installed gateway, not on the saved role, so a solo machine can run them.
- 🤖 **Does the pack keep a workflow?** Yes, one default-on `mcp-gateway` workflow. It carries the page's moment and the old off switch.
- 🤖 **What happens to a key that an older grant wrote with the hub's HTTPS address?** The client check's repair adopts the key whatever address sits beside it, and rewrites the client file at loopback. Without that, existing nodes would lose MCP access at their next update (review round 1).
- 🤖 **What happens to a gateway installed at the hub's HTTPS address?** Its install check fails and names the address, so apply reinstalls it at loopback. Upstream sign-ins and keys stay on disk (review round 1).
- 🤖 **Where do errors that reach `main` go?** To standard error in the real CLI, for every command, so `fleet mcp-connect` never writes one onto the MCP stream. Tests that pass no `fail` still read them through `print` (review round 1).

issue.title: Issue the hub's own credentials during apply, and add ctx.use and Fleet repairs
issue.body:
## Problem

The hub's own MCP bridge needs a key today that a person grants by hand on the hub. Fleet v2 lets each served service issue its own credentials (`docs/architecture.md` D14): the hub asks the service for its own key during apply, and pack code reads it with `ctx.use`. An install step also needs a repair that Fleet runs itself, not a separate shell command.

This is step 2.3 of 4. Merge [#28](https://github.com/Silthus/fleet-engine/pull/28) first.

## Merge Danger

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - `fleet apply` gains two phases: Fleet repairs run before the adapters, and on the hub the credential phase runs after the gate. Both act only on `pack.ts` items that declare a `repair.run` or `serve`; no shipped pack declares either before 2.4, so applies on existing machines are unchanged.
> - A failed issue is a Fix finding and keeps apply's exit code, so a nightly update never stops on it.
> - **Switch-off:** none: live on deploy, fix forward.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Summary

- **Credential phase.** After the gate, `fleet apply` on the hub calls `serve.credential(ctx, <hub name>)` for each catalog service whose gate passed and whose pack's secret store holds no credential, and stores the answer as `credential.<service id>` in that store. A credential that throws or comes back empty stores nothing and gives `Fix: Could not issue the credential of <pack>/<id>: <reason>. Fleet tries again at the next apply.` Nodes issue nothing in this step; stack 3 adds the pull from the hub.
- **`ctx.use(service)`** only reads. It returns `{ url: "http://127.0.0.1:<port>", credential }` from the catalog and the serving pack's secret store, and fails fast with a sentence when the catalog leaves the service out (its workflow or plan is off) or this machine has no credential yet.
- A served service's id names its credential, so register refuses an id that is not lowercase words joined by dashes or dots.
- **`Repair` takes `{ run(ctx) }`**, a repair that Fleet runs during apply when its check fails, then probes again; `fleet run <pack>/<check id> --repair` runs it. A repair is a person's command, which needs `ask`, or a Fleet run, where `ask` is optional. It is never both. `fleet doctor` never runs a repair.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** `src/reconciler/credentials.test.ts` drives `fleet` through `main` on a temporary home with a `pack.ts` fixture whose served service counts the keys it issues. On the hub, the first apply runs the install repair and issues `key-1-for-hub-1`, `fleet issued use` prints `http://127.0.0.1:4600 key-1-for-hub-1`, and a second apply keeps that key. A repair that throws leaves the check as a To do and no key. A service that refuses gives the Fix finding and stores nothing. A node's apply issues nothing, and `ctx.use` fails with its sentence there. A service whose workflow is off is named as missing from the catalog.
- **Red, then green:** the 5 tests failed on #28's head and pass on this head. Mutants that issue on every apply, or that skip the repair, each fail a test.
- **Review fixes, red then green:**
  - The register test for `odd_api` fails before the id rule and passes after it.
  - The issued fixture's Fleet repair has no `ask`. `bun run typecheck` failed on it before the `Repair` union and passes after it.
- **Lane gate:** `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run test` on this head, with `main` merged in: 1656 pass, and 15 fail only on the devbox that built this, as on `main` there: three tracker tests, because its Git allowlist rewrites https origins, and twelve privacy-scan tests, because it has no gitleaks build.
- **CI:** pending on the head.

## Decisions

See the decision comment below.

Involvement: one GPT-6.1 Sol review round. It found three issues: the issue order was fixed in #38's gate, and the id rule and the `Repair` union are fixed here with tests. A second GPT-6.1 Sol round over the stack's fix commits and its merges from `main` found one should-fix, in #28: an outage now also removes a gated key that overlaps an older one. It is fixed with a test. No live proof; Michael's overnight order on 2026-11-10 moves live proofs to follow-ups after the merge.

## For reviewers

PR 3 of 4 for Fleet v2 step 2. 2.4 moves the MCP gateway onto this: its served service issues today's per-machine grant, and its bridge reads the key with `ctx.use`.

**Decision lines** (overnight run: the worker took the recommended option and recorded it here)

- 🤖 **Where does a credential live?** As `credential.<service id>` in the serving pack's secret store. Stack 3's pull stores into the same name.
- 🤖 **What does a failed issue do?** A Fix finding that says Fleet tries again at the next apply. Apply's exit code stays 0, so a nightly update never stops on it, and nothing is stored.
- 🤖 **When do Fleet repairs run?** In apply's gate, before the adapters, through `fleet run <pack>/<check> --repair`. Never in `fleet doctor` or `--dry-run`.
- 🤖 **Can a repair be a person's command and a Fleet run?** No. Register refuses a repair that has both.
- 🤖 **Is a stored key ever issued again?** Not in step 2. Apply issues only when the store holds none. A revoked key is fixed by deleting the stored one; rotation waits for its first user.
- 🤖 **Which ids may a served service have?** Lowercase words joined by dashes or dots, because the id names its credential secret. Register refuses others (review round 1).

issue.title: Build the service catalog, serve, and fleet.config for pack.ts
issue.body:
## Problem

A service on the hub that other nodes use, such as the MCP gateway, is hand-built today: its port lives in a unit, a tunnel, and a config line each. Fleet v2 lets a `pack.ts` declare such a service once with `serve`, and every node computes the same service catalog from the same profile, so a node knows the hub's ports without a discovery daemon (`docs/architecture.md` D11, D12). A pack also needs provider config items that appear only where and when they work.

This is step 2.2 of 4. Merge [#27](https://github.com/Silthus/fleet-engine/pull/27) first.

## Merge Danger

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - `resolve` gains the catalog, and the readiness gate in every `fleet apply` now also tests config items with `after`. No `pack.json` item has `after` on config, and no shipped pack declares `serve`, so today's plans are unchanged apart from an empty catalog.
> - **Switch-off:** none: live on deploy, fix forward.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Summary

- `fleet.service` takes `serve: { port, health, credential }`, all three required. A served service must say `on: "hub"`, and it can omit `run`: Fleet then writes no unit, because something else, such as Docker, keeps it running. A service needs `run`, `serve`, or both.
- `resolve` builds the catalog, `<pack>/<service id>` to port and health path, before it filters items for this machine. It judges `plans` and `when` on the profile, and `os` as the hub's: this machine's on the hub, Linux on any other node. It does not judge `after`. The plan carries the catalog. Two services that claim one port fail at resolve time.
- `fleet.config({ provider, key, value, ...scope })` maps onto today's config entries and their one-owner rule. With `after`, the readiness gate holds the entry back until its check passes, and the provider config adapter removes it when the check stops passing.
- During a source outage, Fleet still removes a provider setting or a Claude MCP server that the gate dropped because its check fails. Everything else that departed stays until every source can be fetched.
- Every node activates the catalog's workflows as the hub would, so a workflow that needs a devbox gives every node the same catalog.
- A profile's `overrides.config` cannot take `after`, because only a pack's own item can name its check.
- A `pack.json` cannot declare `served`, because a credential is code.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** `src/reconciler/catalog.test.ts` loads a `pack.ts` fixture and resolves one profile that names a hub. The node's plan holds the hub's served service in its catalog, the same as the hub's, while the node gets none of the hub's items. The catalog follows the profile's plan and workflows, and a Linux-only served service shows on a Mac node too. Two packs on one port fail, and a `pack.ts` config key has one owner. `register` refuses a served service off the hub, a service with neither `run` nor `serve`, a bad port, and a health path without a leading `/`. Through `fleet apply` with the real provider config adapter, a config item with `after` stays out of `~/.codex/config.toml` until `fleet served install` passes the check, and a hub-only config item never lands on a node.
- **Red, then green:** the 6 tests failed on #27's head and pass on this head. Mutants that judge the os on this machine, or that skip the gate for config, each fail a test.
- **Review fixes, red then green:** each new test fails before its fix and passes after it.
  - In `provider-config.test.ts`, during an outage, a gated `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and a gated Claude MCP server are removed, and a setting the outage hides stays.
  - In `catalog.test.ts`, a plain Linux node lists the same catalog as the hub for a default-on workflow that needs a devbox.
  - In `profile.test.ts`, an override with `after` fails to load.
- **Lane gate:** `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run test` on this head, with `main` merged in: 1651 pass, and 15 fail only on the devbox that built this, as on `main` there: three tracker tests, because its Git allowlist rewrites https origins, and twelve privacy-scan tests, because it has no gitleaks build.
- **CI:** pending on the head.
- Gaps: none beyond the stack's live runs, which follow after merge.

## Decisions

See the decision comment below.

Involvement: one GPT-6.1 Sol review round. It found two blocking bugs and one should-fix, and all three are fixed with tests. A second GPT-6.1 Sol round over the stack's fix commits and its merges from `main` found one should-fix, in #28: an outage now also removes a gated key that overlaps an older one. It is fixed with a test. No live proof; Michael's overnight order on 2026-11-10 moves live proofs to follow-ups after the merge.

issue.title: Name the hub in the profile with fleet hub here
issue.body:
## Problem

Today the hub is whatever machine saved `role: "hub"` in its own `machine.json`, and the Hub pack's `hub.alias` setting holds its SSH name, so the two can disagree and no node can tell from the profile which machine is the hub. Fleet v2 step 2 needs every node to read one answer from the same profile (`docs/architecture.md` D2).

This is step 2.1 of 4 (Fleet v2 step 2, one served hub service). It branches off `main`.

## Merge Danger

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - Every `fleet apply` now saves the machine's name, and `resolve` derives the role from `profile.hub` when the profile names one. A profile without `hub`, which is every profile today, keeps today's placement; the only visible change is a `name` in `machine.json` and a note on a profile that lists devboxes and names no hub.
> - `fleet hub` is now an engine command, so the Hub pack's own `hub` command goes. `fleet hub here` now also writes the profile and pushes it.
> - **Switch-off:** none: live on deploy, fix forward.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Summary

- `fleet.json` takes an optional `hub`: the SSH name of the machine that runs the hub's items. The machine file stores the machine's own `name`. `fleet setup` and `fleet apply` save the host name once when none is saved, so a rerun of apply after setup leaves `machine.json` alone.
- `fleet hub here [<ssh name>]` saves this machine's name and `role: "hub"` (schema 1 packs still read the role, D22), writes `hub` to the profile, pushes it, and applies, the way `fleet set` saves a change. `fleet hub status` prints this machine's name and the hub.
- When the profile names a hub, that name wins over the Hub pack's `hub.alias` setting, so boxes, tunnels, and grants reach the hub that `fleet hub here` named.
- A machine is the hub when `profile.hub` is its name. The profile wins over a saved role, and apply saves the derived role, so schema 1 code that reads `machine.json` follows.
- A profile without `hub` keeps today's placement. A profile that lists devboxes and names no hub leaves out a non-hub machine's hub items, and `fleet apply` and `fleet doctor` add a note that names `fleet hub here`. A profile that names a hub makes no machine solo.
- The machine file is written with the private-file writer (mode 600, random temporary name), the protection the Hub pack's `markHub` had.
- `docs/architecture.md` takes step 2's accepted changes: D2 is built here, and `ctx.node`, `Service.url`, `credentialCommand`, and the optional `serve` fields wait for their first users. `GLOSSARY.md` and the fleet-hub skill describe the hub by the profile.

## Evidence

- **Tests:** `src/commands/hub.test.ts` drives `fleet` through `main` on a temporary home, with a bare Git remote for the profile and a `pack.ts` fixture whose service runs only on the hub. It shows: before `fleet hub here`, `fleet run` refuses the hub's service and names `fleet hub here`, and doctor shows the note; after it, the remote profile holds `hub`, `machine.json` holds the name and `role: "hub"`, the service runs, and the note is gone. A saved hub role that the profile does not name loses to the profile, and apply saves `linux`. The machine the profile names is the hub without a saved role. A profile without hub or devboxes keeps the solo placement. An SSH name argument wins over the host name; a bad name changes nothing; a profile `hub` that is not an SSH name fails to load. A file planted at the old temporary name is not written through.
- **Red, then green:** the hub tests failed on `main` (`4871f89`) and pass on this head. The first install smoke run failed because the rerun of apply rewrote `machine.json`: setup had saved it without the name. The setup test now expects the name; it failed before the fix in `2f94b40` and passes after it. Mutants without the solo rule change, without the role derivation, or without the note each fail a test.
- **Review fixes, red then green:**
  - After `fleet hub here new-hub` on a profile whose `hub.alias` is `old-hub`, `fleet settings` shows `hub.alias = new-hub`. The test fails without the change in `resolve` and passes with it.
  - When apply saves `name: "hub-1"` and `role: "hub"`, setup keeps both when it saves its progress after apply. The test fails without the change and passes with it.
- **Lane gate:** `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run test` on this head, with `main` merged in: 1642 pass, and 15 fail only on the devbox that built this, as on `main` there: three tracker tests, because its Git allowlist rewrites https origins, and twelve privacy-scan tests, because it has no gitleaks build.
- **CI:** pending on the head.
- Gaps: no live run of `fleet hub here` on a real machine; it is a follow-up after merge.

## Decisions

See the decision comment below.

Involvement: one GPT-6.1 Sol review round. It found two blocking bugs, and both are fixed with tests. A second GPT-6.1 Sol round over the stack's fix commits and its merges from `main` found one should-fix, in #28: an outage now also removes a gated key that overlaps an older one. It is fixed with a test. No live proof; Michael's overnight order on 2026-11-10 moves live proofs to follow-ups after the merge.

## For reviewers

This PR is the first of four that land Fleet v2 step 2. Later PRs add the service catalog, the credential phase, and the `mcp-gateway` pack, and change `src/reconciler/resolve.ts`, `src/reconciler/apply.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, and `src/pack/types.ts` again.

+                                return all
+                            }
+                            const nextOffset = Number(

+    reducers({
+        addedFilters: [
+            [] as FacetFilter[],
+            { setAddedFilters: (_, { filters }) => withoutFolderScope(filters), clearSavedViews: () => [] },
+        ],
+        addedText: [null as string | null, { setAddedText: (_, { text }) => text, clearSavedViews: () => null }],
+        savedViewsLoadFailed: [

+        ],
+        defaultView: [

+            upsertSavedView: (state, { view }) =>

+    selectors({

+        available: [

+        ],
+        viewsResolving: [

+        views: [

+                BUILT_IN_WORKFLOW_VIEWS[0],
+                ...(savedViews ?? []).filter((view) => view.default_key === 'my-workflows'),
+                ...BUILT_IN_WORKFLOW_VIEWS.slice(1),
+                ...(savedViews ?? []).filter((view) => view.default_key !== 'my-workflows'),
+            ],
+        ],
+        activeView: [
+            (s) => [s.views, s.activeViewId],
+            (views: WorkflowSavedView[], activeViewId: string): WorkflowSavedView =>
+                views.find((view) => view.id === activeViewId) ?? BUILT_IN_WORKFLOW_VIEWS[0],
+        ],
+        activeViewChanges: [
+            (s) => [s.activeView, s.value, s.shownColumns],
+            (view: WorkflowSavedView, value: FacetSearchValue, columns: OptionalColumn[]): string[] =>
+                savedViewChanges(view, value, columns),
+        ],
+        isModified: [(s) => [s.activeViewChanges], (changes: string[]): boolean => changes.length > 0],
+        hasAdditions: [
+            (s) => [s.addedFilters, s.addedText],
+            (addedFilters: FacetFilter[], addedText: string | null): boolean =>
+                addedFilters.length > 0 || addedText !== null,
+        ],
+        canUpdateActiveView: [(s) => [s.activeView], (view: WorkflowSavedView): boolean => !view.builtIn],
+        activeViewConflicted: [
+            (s) => [s.conflictedViewId, s.activeViewId],
+            (conflictedViewId: string | null, activeViewId: string): boolean => conflictedViewId === activeViewId,
+        ],
+        sharedSaveDisabledReason: [
+            (s) => [s.activeViewConflicted],
+            (activeViewConflicted: boolean): string | undefined =>
+                activeViewConflicted ? 'Reset to the latest version of this view before you update it' : undefined,
+        ],
+        myWorkflowsDeleted: [(s) => [s.defaultView], (view: WorkflowViewApi | null): boolean => view?.deleted === true],
+        saving: [(s) => [s.pendingAction], (pendingAction: SavedViewAction | null): boolean => pendingAction !== null],
+        viewCounts: [
+            (s) => [s.views, s.rows, s.facetsFor, s.matchesText, s.serverSearch, s.metricsLoaded, s.listLoaded],
+            (
+                views: WorkflowSavedView[],
+                rows: WorkflowListRow[],
+                facetsFor: (value: FacetSearchValue) => FacetDefinition<WorkflowListRow>[],
+                matchesText: MatchesText<WorkflowListRow>,
+                serverSearch: ServerSearchResult | null,
+                metricsLoaded: boolean,
+                listLoaded: boolean
+            ): Record<string, number> =>
+                !listLoaded
+                    ? {}
+                    : Object.fromEntries(
+                          views.flatMap((view) => {
+                              if (!metricsLoaded && view.state.filters.some((filter) => filter.facet === 'health')) {
+                                  return []
+                              }
+                              const text = view.state.text.trim()
+                              if (
+                                  text.length >= MIN_SERVER_SEARCH_LENGTH &&
+                                  (serverSearch?.text !== text || serverSearch.failed)
+                              ) {
+                                  return []
+                              }
+                              const value = workflowViewValue(view.state)
+                              return [
+                                  [
+                                      view.id,
+                                      rows.filter(createFacetMatcher(value, facetsFor(value), matchesText)).length,
+                                  ],
+                              ]
+                          })
+                      ),
+        ],
+    }),
+    listeners(({ actions, values, cache }) => {
+        const writeUrl = (): void => {
+            if (!values.available || cache.applyingView || cache.syncingUrl) {
+                return
+            }
+            const next: Record<string, unknown> = {
+                ...router.values.searchParams,
+                view: values.activeViewId,
+                q: serializeFacetQuery(values.value.filters),
+                text: values.value.text.trim(),
+                columns: values.shownColumns.join(','),
+                added: serializeFacetQuery(values.addedFilters),
+            }
+            delete next.typed
+            if (values.addedText !== null) {
+                next.typed = '1'
+            }
+            const raw = new URLSearchParams(router.values.location.search)
+            if (
+                raw.get('view') === next.view &&
+                raw.get('q') === next.q &&
+                raw.get('text') === next.text &&
+                raw.get('columns') === next.columns &&
+                (raw.get('added') ?? '') === next.added &&
+                raw.get('typed') === (next.typed ?? null)
+            ) {
+                return
+            }
+            cache.writingUrl = true
+            router.actions.replace(router.values.location.pathname, next, router.values.hashParams)
+            cache.writingUrl = false
+        }
+        const userText = (text: string): string | null => (text.trim() ? text : null)
+        const clearAddedFiltersUnless = (keepAddedFilters: boolean): void => {
+            if (!keepAddedFilters) {
+                actions.setAddedFilters([])
+                actions.setAddedText(null)
+            }
+        }
+        const ignoreMissingView = (error: unknown): void => {
+            if (!isMissingViewError(error)) {
+                throw error
+            }
+        }
+        const pillKey = (filter: FacetFilter): string => facetFilterKey(filter, values.facets)
+        const additionTrackers = (): Set<Set<string>> => (cache.additionTrackers ??= new Set<Set<string>>())
+        const trackAdditions = (): Set<string> => {
+            const added = new Set<string>()
+            additionTrackers().add(added)
+            return added
+        }
+        const rememberAddedFilters = (previous: FacetFilter[], next: FacetFilter[]): void => {
+            const previousKeys = new Set(previous.map(pillKey))
+            for (const filter of next) {
+                if (!previousKeys.has(pillKey(filter))) {
+                    for (const added of additionTrackers()) {
+                        added.add(pillKey(filter))
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        const keepAdditionsMadeSinceSubmit = (saved: WorkflowViewApi, added: Set<string>): void => {
+            actions.setAddedFilters(
+                addedFiltersAfterEdit(
+                    workflowViewValue(saved.state).filters,
+                    values.value.filters.filter((filter) => added.has(pillKey(filter))),
+                    values.value.filters,
+                    values.facets
+                )
+            )
+            actions.setAddedText(
+                values.value.text.trim() !== saved.state.text.trim() ? userText(values.value.text) : null
+            )
+        }
+        const removeDeletedView = (id: string): void => {
+            actions.removeSavedView(id)
+            if (values.defaultView?.id === id) {
+                actions.setDefaultView({ ...values.defaultView, deleted: true })
+            }
+        }
+        const forgetDeletedView = (id: string): void => {
+            removeDeletedView(id)
+            if (values.conflictedViewId === id) {
+                actions.setConflictedViewId(null)
+            }
+            if (values.activeViewId === id) {
+                actions.setAddedFilters(values.value.filters)
+                actions.setAddedText(userText(values.value.text))
+                actions.setActiveViewId(BUILT_IN_WORKFLOW_VIEWS[0].id)
+            }
+        }
+        const handleFailure = (action: SavedViewAction, error: unknown, target?: WorkflowSavedView): unknown => {
+            lemonToast.error(savedViewFailureMessage(action, target?.name ?? 'this view', error))
+            if (target && error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 409) {
+                actions.setConflictedViewId(target.id)
+                return null
+            }
+            if (target && isMissingViewError(error)) {
+                forgetDeletedView(target.id)
+                return null
+            }
+            return error
+        }
+        const executeMutation = async (
+            action: SavedViewAction,
+            run: (stillCurrent: () => boolean) => Promise<void>,
+            generation: number,
+            teamId: number | null,
+            target?: WorkflowSavedView,
+            onFailure?: (failure: unknown) => void
+        ): Promise<void> => {
+            const stillCurrent = (): boolean =>
+                (cache.contextGeneration ?? 0) === generation && values.enabled && values.currentTeamId === teamId
+            if (!stillCurrent() || !values.available) {
+                return
+            }
+            actions.setPendingAction(action)
+            try {
+                await run(stillCurrent)
+            } catch (error) {
+                if (stillCurrent()) {
+                    const failure = handleFailure(action, error, target)
+                    if (failure) {
+                        onFailure?.(failure)
+                    }
+                }
+            } finally {
+                if (stillCurrent()) {
+                    actions.setPendingAction(null)
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        const runMutation = (
+            action: SavedViewAction,
+            key: string,
+            run: (stillCurrent: () => boolean) => Promise<void>,
+            target?: WorkflowSavedView,
+            onFailure?: (failure: unknown) => void
+        ): Promise<void> => {
+            const needsWriteAccess = action !== 'reset'
+            if (!values.available || (needsWriteAccess && values.writeDisabledReason)) {
+                return Promise.resolve()
+            }
+            const generation = cache.contextGeneration ?? 0
+            if (cache.mutationQueueGeneration !== generation) {
+                cache.mutationQueueGeneration = generation
+                cache.mutationQueue = Promise.resolve()
+                cache.mutationKeys = new Set<string>()
+            }
+            const keys: Set<string> = cache.mutationKeys
+            const queueKey = `${action}:${key}`
+            if (keys.has(queueKey)) {
+                return Promise.resolve()
+            }
+            keys.add(queueKey)
+            const teamId = values.currentTeamId
+            const execute = async (): Promise<void> => {
+                try {
+                    await executeMutation(action, run, generation, teamId, target, onFailure)
+                } finally {
+                    keys.delete(queueKey)
+                }
+            }
+            const queued = keys.size === 1 ? execute() : (cache.mutationQueue as Promise<void>).then(execute)
+            cache.mutationQueue = queued
+            return queued
+        }
+        const latestVersion = (view: WorkflowSavedView): number =>
+            values.views.find((candidate) => candidate.id === view.id)?.version ?? view.version
+        return {
+            clearSavedViews: () => {
+                cache.contextGeneration = (cache.contextGeneration ?? 0) + 1
+            },
+            setFeatureFlags: () => {
+                if (!values.enabled) {
+                    actions.clearSavedViews()
+                    actions.loadSavedViews()
+                } else if (values.savedViews === null && !values.savedViewsLoading) {
+                    actions.loadSavedViews()
+                }
+            },
+            loadCurrentTeamSuccess: ({ currentTeam }) => {
+                if (cache.loadedTeamId !== currentTeam?.id) {
+                    cache.loadedTeamId = currentTeam?.id
+                    actions.clearSavedViews()
+                    actions.loadSavedViews()
+                }
+            },
+            loadSavedViewsSuccess: () => actions.syncViewFromUrl(),
+            setValue: ({ value, fromUrl }, _, __, previousState) => {
+                if (!fromUrl) {
+                    if (values.available && !cache.applyingView && !cache.syncingUrl) {
+                        const previous = workflowsListV2Logic.selectors.value(previousState)
+                        actions.setAddedFilters(
+                            addedFiltersAfterEdit(previous.filters, values.addedFilters, value.filters, values.facets)
+                        )
+                        rememberAddedFilters(previous.filters, value.filters)
+                        if (value.text !== previous.text) {
+                            actions.setAddedText(userText(value.text))
+                        }
+                    }
+                    writeUrl()
+                }
+            },
+            setActiveViewId: writeUrl,
+            clearFilters: () => {
+                actions.setAddedFilters([])
+                actions.setAddedText(null)
+                writeUrl()
+            },
+            setVisibleColumns: writeUrl,
+            toggleColumn: writeUrl,
+            resetColumns: writeUrl,
+            applyView: ({ view }) => {
+                if (!values.available) {
+                    return
+                }
+                cache.applyingView = true
+                const viewValue = workflowViewValue(view.state)
+                actions.setValue({
+                    filters: mergeAddedFilters(viewValue.filters, values.addedFilters, values.facets),
+                    text: values.addedText ?? viewValue.text,
+                })
+                actions.setVisibleColumns(normalizeViewColumns(view.state.columns))
+                cache.applyingView = false
+                writeUrl()
+                if (values.conflictedViewId === view.id) {
+                    actions.resetView(true)
+                }
+            },
+            resetView: async ({ keepAddedFilters }) => {
+                if (!values.available || values.saving) {
+                    return
+                }
+                if (values.activeViewConflicted) {
+                    const currentViewId = values.activeViewId
+                    const startValue = values.value
+                    const startColumns = values.shownColumns
+                    const editedWhileLoading = (): boolean =>
+                        values.value !== startValue || values.shownColumns !== startColumns
+                    await runMutation(
+                        'reset',
+                        currentViewId,
+                        async (stillCurrent) => {
+                            try {
+                                const latest = await api.workflowViewsRetrieve(
+                                    String(values.currentTeamId),
+                                    currentViewId
+                                )
+                                if (!stillCurrent()) {
+                                    return
+                                }
+                                actions.upsertSavedView(latest)
+                                actions.setConflictedViewId(null)
+                                if (values.activeViewId === currentViewId && !editedWhileLoading()) {
+                                    clearAddedFiltersUnless(keepAddedFilters)
+                                    actions.applyView(latest)
+                                }
+                            } catch (error) {
+                                if (!isMissingViewError(error)) {
+                                    throw error
+                                }
+                                if (!stillCurrent()) {
+                                    return
+                                }
+                                if (editedWhileLoading()) {
+                                    forgetDeletedView(currentViewId)
+                                    return
+                                }
+                                removeDeletedView(currentViewId)
+                                if (values.activeViewId === currentViewId) {
+                                    clearAddedFiltersUnless(keepAddedFilters)
+                                    actions.applyView(BUILT_IN_WORKFLOW_VIEWS[0])
+                                }
+                            }
+                            actions.setConflictedViewId(null)
+                        },
+                        values.activeView
+                    )
+                } else {
+                    clearAddedFiltersUnless(keepAddedFilters)
+                    actions.applyView(values.activeView)
+                }
+            },
+            syncViewFromUrl: () => {
+                const raw = new URLSearchParams(router.values.location.search)
+                const id = raw.get('view') ?? 'all'
+                const explicit = raw.has('q') || raw.has('text') || raw.has('columns') || raw.has('added')
+                if (!values.available) {
+                    if (values.enabled && raw.has('view') && !explicit && cache.viewOnlyLink?.id !== id) {
+                        cache.viewOnlyLink = { id, baseline: values.value }
+                    }
+                    return
+                }
+                if (cache.writingUrl || cache.applyingView) {
+                    return
+                }
+                const view = values.views.find((candidate) => candidate.id === id)
+                const viewOnlyLink: { id: string; baseline: FacetSearchValue } | undefined = cache.viewOnlyLink
+                cache.viewOnlyLink = undefined
+                if (view && viewOnlyLink?.id === id) {
+                    const edited = values.value
+                    const baselineKeys = new Set(viewOnlyLink.baseline.filters.map(pillKey))
+                    actions.setAddedFilters(edited.filters.filter((filter) => !baselineKeys.has(pillKey(filter))))
+                    actions.setAddedText(null)
+                    actions.applyView(view)
+                    if (edited.text !== viewOnlyLink.baseline.text) {
+                        actions.setValue({ ...values.value, text: edited.text })
+                    }
+                    return
+                }
+                if (view && !explicit) {
+                    actions.setAddedFilters([])
+                    actions.setAddedText(null)
+                    actions.applyView(view)
+                    return
+                }
+                cache.syncingUrl = true
+                actions.setActiveViewId(view?.id ?? 'all')
+                if (explicit) {
+                    const value: FacetSearchValue = {
+                        filters: raw.has('q')
+                            ? parseFacetQuery(raw.get('q') ?? '', values.facets)
+                            : view
+                              ? workflowViewValue(view.state).filters
+                              : [],
+                        text: raw.has('text') ? (raw.get('text') ?? '') : (view?.state.text ?? ''),
+                    }
+                    actions.setValue(value)
+                    const typed = raw.get('typed') === '1' || value.text.trim() !== (view?.state.text ?? '').trim()
+                    actions.setAddedText(typed ? userText(value.text) : null)
+                    const effectiveKeys = new Set(value.filters.map(pillKey))
+                    actions.setAddedFilters(
+                        raw.has('added')
+                            ? parseFacetQuery(raw.get('added') ?? '', values.facets).filter((filter) =>
+                                  effectiveKeys.has(pillKey(filter))
+                              )

issue.title: chore(skills): add node level, mutation check, and outcome rules to writing-tests
issue.body:
## Problem

- Agents that follow [#132618](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/132618) still copy mock harnesses in four places it leaves open.
- Node CDP tests carry the most mock assertions, and the cost ladder has no Node level.
- Nothing asks the agent to prove a test fails when the code breaks.

## Changes

A proposal for DevEx review, stacked on #132618.

- Node gets a level and a section: enter through `createHub`, assert what a boundary recorded, keep case matrices out of the serial lane.
- Gate question 3: break the guarded line and watch the test fail.
- A request or message that a boundary fake recorded counts as an outcome.
- A test takes a real dependency only when the behavior uses it.
- A boundary stub may return a canned success, not only a fault.
- The skill prose loses em dashes and most prohibitions. Its rules stay the same.
- The handbook, `.claude/commands/conventions.md`, and `test-writer` match.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** No tests. Guidance only.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- The handbook Testing section changes in this PR.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

**Skills:** `/writing-skills`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/stacking-prs`, `council`, `unslop`, `writing-for-agents`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** T3 Code thread, Claude Code with git and gh.
- **Decisions:** Kept the "cost ladder", "the gate", and "extract, don't escalate" names, because other skills cite them.
- **Decisions:** Dropped the "each rung is an order of magnitude slower" ratio, because no repo timing supports it.
- **Read closely:** "What counts as an outcome" and the "No real network" bullet carry the relaxed stub rule.

</details>

+            rows = connection.execute("SELECT app, name FROM django_migrations").fetchall()
+        return {MigrationReference(app=app, name=name) for app, name in rows}
+
+    def forget_migrations(self, dbname: str, apps: list[str]) -> None:
+        with self.connect(dbname) as connection:
+            connection.execute("DELETE FROM django_migrations WHERE app = ANY(%s)", (apps,))
+
+    def load_gzip_dump(self, dbname: str, dump: Path) -> None:
+        psql = shutil.which("psql")
+        if psql is None:
+            run_psql_with_gzip_input(dump, dbname)
+            return
+        connection = ["-h", self.host, "-p", self.port, "-U", self.user, dbname]
+        with gzip.open(dump, "rb") as source:
+            subprocess.run(
+                [psql, "-q", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "--single-transaction", *connection],
+                input=source.read(),
+                env={**os.environ, "PGPASSWORD": self.password},
+                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                check=True,
+            )
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def build_lock(self) -> Iterator[None]:
+        with self.connect("postgres") as admin:
+            admin.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(%s)", (TEMPLATE_BUILD_LOCK,))
+            try:
+                yield
+            finally:
+                admin.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(%s)", (TEMPLATE_BUILD_LOCK,))
+
+    def _admin(self, statement: sql.Composed) -> None:
+        with self.connect("postgres") as admin:
+            admin.execute(statement)
+
+
+class Checkout:
+    def __init__(self, root: Path = REPO_ROOT, *, master_ref: str = "origin/master") -> None:
+        self.root = root
+        self.master_ref = master_ref
+        self._contains: dict[str, bool] = {}
+
+    def contains(self, sha: str) -> bool:
+        if sha not in self._contains:
+            self._contains[sha] = self._git("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", sha, "HEAD") is not None
+        return self._contains[sha]
+
+    def lags_master_base(self, sha: str, *, by_seconds: int) -> bool:
+        """Whether sha is older than the master commit this checkout last merged, by more than by_seconds."""
+        base = self._git("merge-base", "HEAD", self.master_ref) or "HEAD"
+        base_time, sha_time = self._commit_time(base), self._commit_time(sha)
+        return base_time is None or sha_time is None or base_time - sha_time > by_seconds
+
+    def _commit_time(self, revision: str) -> int | None:
+        output = self._git("show", "-s", "--format=%ct", revision)
+        return int(output) if output else None
+
+    def _git(self, *args: str) -> str | None:
+        result = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=self.root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
+        return result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else None
+
+
+class TemplateStore:
+    """Migrated template databases on one Postgres server, one per master commit that CI dumped."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        server: PostgresServer,
+        checkout: Checkout,
+        *,
+        allow_download: bool = True,
+        prefix: str = TEMPLATE_PREFIX,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.server = server
+        self.checkout = checkout
+        self.allow_download = allow_download
+        self.prefix = prefix
+
+    def name_for(self, sha: str) -> str:
+        return self.prefix + sha[:TEMPLATE_SHA_LENGTH]
+
+    def usable_template(self) -> str | None:
+        with self.server.build_lock():
+            local = self._newest_local_template()
+            if not self.allow_download or (local is not None and not self._lags_master(local)):
+                return local
+            try:
+                built = self._build_from_newest_artifact()
+            except Exception:
+                if local is None:
+                    raise
+                return local
+            self._prune(keep=built)
+            return built
+
+    def build(self, name: str, dump: Path) -> None:
+        check_dump_is_not_newer_than_checkout(dump)
+        building = name + BUILDING_SUFFIX
+        self.server.drop_database(building)
+        self.server.create_database(building)
+        try:
+            self.server.load_gzip_dump(building, dump)
+            if apps := product_routed_app_labels():
+                self.server.forget_migrations(building, apps)
+            self.server.rename_database(building, name)
+        except Exception:
+            self.server.drop_database(building)
+            raise
+
+    def _newest_local_template(self) -> str | None:
+        for name in self.server.newest_databases_named(self.prefix):
+            if not name.endswith(BUILDING_SUFFIX) and self.checkout.contains(name.removeprefix(self.prefix)):
+                return name
+        return None
+
+    def _lags_master(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        sha = name.removeprefix(self.prefix)
+        return self.checkout.lags_master_base(sha, by_seconds=TEMPLATE_MAX_LAG_SECONDS)
+
+    def _build_from_newest_artifact(self) -> str:
+        token = github_token()
+        session = github_session()
+        artifact = find_newest_compatible_artifact(
+            token=token, session=session, accept=lambda candidate: self.checkout.contains(candidate.head_sha)
+        )
+        if artifact is None:
+            raise TemplateUnavailable("no recent master schema dump is an ancestor of this checkout")
+        name = self.name_for(artifact.head_sha)
+        if not self.server.database_exists(name):
+            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="test-db-template-") as scratch:
+                dump = Path(scratch) / "schema.sql.gz"
+                download_schema_artifact(artifact, token=token, destination=dump, session=session)
+                self.build(name, dump)
+        return name
+
+    def _prune(self, *, keep: str) -> None:
+        older = [name for name in self.server.newest_databases_named(self.prefix) if name != keep][TEMPLATES_KEPT - 1 :]
+        for name in older:
+            try:
+                self.server.drop_database(name)
+            except psycopg.Error:
+                continue
+
+
+class PrimeOutcome(StrEnum):
+    KEPT = "kept"
+    CLONED = "cloned"
+    SKIPPED = "skipped"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True, slots=True)
+class PrimeResult:
+    outcome: PrimeOutcome
+    detail: str
+
+
+def prime_test_database(server: PostgresServer, target_db: str, store: TemplateStore) -> PrimeResult:
+    """Leave target_db ready for Django's keepdb migrate, cloning a template when it holds nothing usable."""
+    exists = server.database_exists(target_db)
+    if exists:
+        recorded = server.recorded_migrations(target_db)
+        missing = migrations_missing_from_checkout(recorded)
+        if recorded and not missing:
+            return PrimeResult(outcome=PrimeOutcome.KEPT, detail=f"{target_db} fits this checkout")
+    template = store.usable_template()
+    if template is None:
+        return PrimeResult(outcome=PrimeOutcome.SKIPPED, detail="no template database is available")
+    if exists:
+        try:
+            server.drop_database(target_db)
+        except psycopg.errors.ObjectInUse:
+            reason = f"records {len(missing)} migrations this checkout lacks" if missing else "has no migrations"
+            return PrimeResult(outcome=PrimeOutcome.SKIPPED, detail=f"{target_db} {reason} and another session uses it")
+    server.create_database(target_db, template=template)
+    return PrimeResult(outcome=PrimeOutcome.CLONED, detail=f"cloned {target_db} from {template}")
+
+
+def prime_django_test_database(default_db: Mapping[str, Any]) -> PrimeResult | None:
+    """Prime the test database of Django's default alias. Off in CI, which restores its own."""
+    if os.environ.get(MODE_ENV, "off" if os.environ.get("CI") else "auto") == "off":
+        return None
+    server = PostgresServer(
+        host=default_db.get("HOST") or "localhost",
+        port=str(default_db.get("PORT") or "5432"),
+        user=default_db.get("USER") or "posthog",
+        password=default_db.get("PASSWORD") or "",
+    )

issue.title: Start pack hooks on SessionStart and Codex PreToolUse, and keep a settings snapshot for them
issue.body:
## Problem

Pack hooks cannot read a setting: only pack commands get `FLEET_SETTINGS`, and hooks start from Claude Code or Codex. Codex also never ran Fleet's PreToolUse hooks, and neither agent ran a SessionStart hook. The guard and memory hooks that come next need all three.

This is 1 of 3 PRs that give the Base pack what those hooks stand on. It merges first.

## Merge Danger

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🔵 **Merge risk: low** · two-way door
> - Nothing changes on a machine until `fleet apply` runs there. Then Claude and Codex start the unchanged dispatcher on two more events, and its event folders are empty until a pack adds a hook. The two PreToolUse hooks that exist today exit at once for Codex.
> - The snapshot is a new file under `~/.local/state/fleet/`, mode 600, that nothing reads yet.
> - **Switch-off:** none: live on apply, fix forward.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Summary

- The Base pack adds `hooks.SessionStart` for Claude and Codex and `hooks.PreToolUse` for Codex, each with the same `run.sh` command as today's entries. The dispatcher does not change.
- A new Base command, `fleet settings-snapshot`, writes the resolved settings to `~/.local/state/fleet/settings.json` with mode 600. It writes to a temporary file and renames it, so a hook never reads half a file. With `--check` it exits 1 when the file differs or others can read it.
- A Base step runs it first on every apply, with `--check` as its check, so the file follows a changed setting and is left alone otherwise. It runs before the agent CLI installers, so a failed install does not skip it.

## Evidence

- **Live run, real CLI on a temporary `HOME`:** `main`'s engine applied first, then this head on the same home. The second apply wrote `settings.json` with mode `600`, and `fleet doctor` said "Everything matches your profile." After `base.heavySlots` changed in the profile, `doctor` said "Step settings-snapshot of the base pack does not pass its check." Then `apply` wrote `"base.heavySlots": 3`, and `doctor` was clean again. The hook commands that apply installed in `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/config.toml` passed a SessionStart input (Claude and Codex) and a Codex PreToolUse input to a fixture hook, exit 0.
- **Tests:** `packs/base/apply.test.ts` drives the CLI's `main` on a temporary `HOME`. It reads the hook commands that apply installed and runs them with a fixture hook in the event folder. It also checks that the snapshot follows a changed setting and that a snapshot others can read is written again. Steps other than `fleet …` return 0 there, so no agent CLI installer runs. Mutants that skip the mode check or make `--check` always pass each fail a test.
- **Lane gate:** `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run test` passes everything except tests that fail on `main` on the devbox that built this stack: 3 tracker tests, because the devbox's Git allowlist rewrites https origins, and 12 privacy-scan tests, because it has no arm64 gitleaks. Two prune tests hit their 5-second timeout once while other work loaded the devbox (load average about 14), and passed alone. The suite took 7 to 9 seconds there, as `main` did.
- **CI:** pending on the head.
- Test seams: the CLI's `main` and the hook commands that apply installs. Gap: no real Claude Code or Codex session fired the hooks, because the temporary `HOME` has no agent sign-in. The proof runs the command those agents run.

## Decisions

| Question | Answer | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What is the snapshot step called? | `fleet settings-snapshot`, a Base pack command, because `fleet settings` is a core command in `src/cli.ts`, which another in-flight stack owns | 🤖 Agent | [decisions](https://github.com/Silthus/fleet-engine/pull/11#issuecomment-6768660802) |
| When is the snapshot written again? | When its content differs or its mode is not 600 | 🤖 Agent | [decisions](https://github.com/Silthus/fleet-engine/pull/11#issuecomment-6768660802) |

Involvement: one design pass (Design and Anti-Overengineering, GPT-6.1 Sol), both findings fixed. Proof captured.

## For reviewers

The next two PRs stack on this one: a Linux session file for agent shells and cron, then an hourly night retry for the update jobs. The guard and memory packs read `~/.local/state/fleet/settings.json` and add hooks to the new events. A design that they would have to undo is a finding too.
